title: CPU, RAM, and Persistent Storage
instructions: Answer from the lesson. For short-answer and practical items, equivalent technically correct wording/code earns credit.

questions.explanation: The CPU fetches and executes instructions; RAM holds active instructions and data.

questions.prompt: What is the key difference between RAM and persistent storage?

options.text: RAM is normally volatile; persistent storage retains data without power

questions.explanation: RAM is working memory and is normally volatile; SSDs/HDDs retain stored data.

questions.prompt: Trace the path from a saved program file to running instructions.
questions.expected_answer: The OS loads program code and required data into memory; the CPU executes instructions and uses registers/caches/RAM while the process runs.
questions.explanation: This tests the lesson’s central data-flow objective.

questions.prompt: A value exists only in a variable and the computer loses power. Is it guaranteed to survive? Why?
questions.expected_answer: In-memory process state is normally lost on power failure; a saved file or durable database write is needed for persistence.

questions.prompt: What role can CPU cache play?
questions.expected_answer: Cache reduces average latency for data/instructions that can be reused; exact behavior depends on hardware and workload.
questions.explanation: Checks understanding without requiring universal timing figures.
